title: "Assignments"

The course includes five cumulative problem sets. Each problem set develops one focal analysis and asks students to connect that analysis to a linguistic question.

## Problem sets

| Assignment | Linguistic data | Statistical content |
|---|---|---|
| [PS1](../problem-sets/ps1/ps1.qmd) | Hillenbrand vowel acoustics | [inference for a paired mean difference](../statistical-inference/paired-mean-inference.qmd) and speaker-level resampling |
| [PS2](../problem-sets/ps2/ps2.qmd) | Provo Corpus eye movements | [grouped cross-validation](../model-criticism-and-prediction/grouped-cross-validation.qmd) and passage-level loss comparisons |
| [PS3](../problem-sets/ps3/ps3-dative-alternation.qmd) | English dative alternation | [logistic regression](../regression-models/logistic-regression.qmd) and leave-one-verb-out evaluation |
| [PS4](../problem-sets/ps4/ps4.qmd) | CommitmentBank projection judgments | [ordinal mixed models](../regression-models/ordinal-mixed-models.qmd), prior and posterior checks, and discourse-grouped validation |
| [PS5](../problem-sets/ps5/ps5.qmd) | PHOIBLE phoneme inventories | [singular value decomposition](../factorization/singular-value-decomposition.qmd) and balanced held-out reconstruction |

## What students should expect

Each problem set is also an assigned reading. It develops the mathematical background and linguistic motivation before asking students to extend the analysis. The relevant note pages link to the precise problem-set sections that students should read and explain why those sections are included. Students submit the completed notebook and must be prepared to explain the analysis during the in-class assessment.
